flowElements.headingText: What this prototype covers, and what it leaves out
flowElements.rawXml:
What this prototype covers, and what it leaves out

What this prototype covers: the standard deduction, exemptions, the age deduction, the filing threshold, the rate schedule, withholding, four Schedule ADJ items (unemployment benefits, military basic pay, military benefits and Commonwealth Savers contributions), the Credit for Low-Income Individuals and both Virginia Earned Income Credits, the locality code and the consumer's use tax (Va. Code §§ 58.1-320, 58.1-321, 58.1-322.02, 58.1-322.03, 58.1-339.8). What it leaves out: itemized deductions, the other additions and subtractions, the other credits, part-year and nonresident returns, and a spouse's share of anything.

Started on another device?

Choose the answers file you downloaded from the review screen. It replaces everything entered here with what is in the file.

Line 4, age deduction:

A filer born on or before January 1, 1939 subtracts $12,000; a filer 65 or older born later subtracts $12,000 less $1 for each $1 of adjusted federal AGI over the threshold for the filing status (§ 58.1-322.03(5)). Your share: . Your spouse's share: .

Line 4 shows $0 because the return claims a low-income credit instead, which the law does not allow alongside the age deduction. See Line 23.

Line 7, Schedule ADJ subtractions:

Three subtractions added up: unemployment benefits (code 37, the 1099-G total less anything repaid), military basic pay (code 38, all of it up to $15,000, shrinking to nothing at $30,000) and military benefits (code 60, up to $30,000 and no more than the taxable amount on your 1099-Rs).

The basic pay subtraction shows $0 because the return claims a low-income credit instead. See Line 23.

Line 12, exemptions:

× for you, a spouse on a joint return and each dependent, , plus × for each of you who is 65 or older or blind, (§ 58.1-322.03(2)).

The 65 or older and blind part is left off because the return claims a low-income credit instead. See Line 23.

Line 16, Virginia income tax:

Virginia taxes the first of taxable income at %, the part up to at %, the part up to at % and the rest at % (§ 58.1-320). Your taxable income of is above : the of tax at that point plus % of , , rounded to the dollar.

Line 16 is $0 all the same: your Virginia adjusted gross income is below the filing threshold for your filing status (§ 58.1-321).

flowElements.headingText: Line 23, credit for low-income workers and families:
flowElements.rawXml:
Line 23, credit for low-income workers and families:

No credit is claimed on this return.

Refundable Virginia Earned Income Credit:

15% of the earned income credit on your federal return. Virginia pays it even when it is more than your tax, so it can become a refund.

Virginia Earned Income Credit:

20% of the earned income credit on your federal return, up to your Virginia tax. That was worth more than the refundable 15% ( ).

Credit for Low-Income Individuals:

$300 for each person in your household, because your family's Virginia adjusted gross income is at or under the poverty guideline for its size. Up to your Virginia tax.

To claim it, your return gives up your age deduction. The credit lowers your tax more.

To claim it, your return gives up your exemption for being 65 or older or blind. The credit lowers your tax more.

To claim it, your return gives up your military basic pay subtraction. The credit lowers your tax more.

You did not have to ask for this. Virginia's three credits for people with low incomes come from your federal return; the return claims the one worth the most to you, as Form 760 asks (Schedule ADJ, Lines 10 to 17).

You could claim in Virginia's credit for low-income workers and families, but only by giving up your age deduction, your 65 or older or blind exemption, or your military basic pay subtraction. Keeping them lowers your tax more, so your return keeps them.

Line 33, consumer's use tax:

of purchases on which no Virginia sales tax was paid, times the % rate for , rounded to the dollar (2024 Form 760 instructions, Line 33).

You bought nothing without paying Virginia sales tax, so Line 33 is $0.

facts.name: Employer's name
facts.description: The employer's name as appears in box c of Form W-2.
facts.rawXml:
<Fact path="/formW2s/*/employerName">
  <Name>Employer's name</Name>
  <Description>The employer's name as appears in box c of Form W-2.</Description>
  <Export downstreamFacts="true"/>
  <Writable>
    <String/>
    <Limit type="Match">
      <String>(([A-Za-z0-9#\-\(\)]|&|')\s?)*([A-Za-z0-9#\-\(\)]|&|')</String>
    </Limit>
    <Limit type="MaxLength">
      <Int>75</Int>
    </Limit>
  </Writable>
</Fact>

facts.name: Form 760 Line 23, Credit for Low-Income Individuals or Virginia Earned Income Credit
facts.description: Schedule ADJ Line 17 when the return claims it; otherwise $0.
facts.rawXml:
<Fact path="/vaLowIncomeCredit">
  <Name>Form 760 Line 23, Credit for Low-Income Individuals or Virginia Earned Income Credit</Name>
  <Description>Schedule ADJ Line 17 when the return claims it; otherwise $0.</Description>
  <Derived>
    <Switch>
      <Case>
        <When>
          <Dependency path="/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit"/>
        </When>
        <Then>
          <Dependency path="/vaBestLowIncomeCredit"/>
        </Then>
      </Case>
      <Case>
        <When>
          <True/>
        </When>
        <Then>
          <Dollar>0</Dollar>
        </Then>
      </Case>
    </Switch>
  </Derived>
</Fact>

facts.name: Form 760 Line 12, exemptions
facts.description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(2): Section A plus Section B, or Section A alone when the return claims a low-income credit.
facts.rawXml:
<Fact path="/vaExemptions">
  <Name>Form 760 Line 12, exemptions</Name>
  <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(2): Section A plus Section B, or Section A alone when the
        return claims a low-income credit.</Description>
  <Derived>
    <Switch>
      <Case>
        <When>
          <Dependency module="virginiaCredits" path="/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit"/>
        </When>
        <Then>
          <Dependency path="/vaPersonalExemptions"/>
        </Then>
      </Case>
      <Case>
        <When>
          <True/>
        </When>
        <Then>
          <Dependency path="/vaWithoutCreditExemptions"/>
        </Then>
      </Case>
    </Switch>
  </Derived>
</Fact>

facts.name: Form 760 Line 4, age deduction
facts.description: Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(D)(5): a return on which the filer or the spouse claims the age deduction cannot claim the Credit for Low-Income Individuals or either Virginia Earned Income Credit. The age deduction the return qualifies for, or $0 when the return claims one of those credits instead.
facts.rawXml:
<Fact path="/vaAgeDeduction">
  <Name>Form 760 Line 4, age deduction</Name>
  <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(D)(5): a return on which the filer or the spouse claims the age
        deduction cannot claim the Credit for Low-Income Individuals or either Virginia Earned Income
        Credit. The age deduction the return qualifies for, or $0 when the return claims one of those
        credits instead.</Description>
  <Derived>
    <Switch>
      <Case>
        <When>
          <Dependency module="virginiaCredits" path="/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit"/>
        </When>
        <Then>
          <Dollar>0</Dollar>
        </Then>
      </Case>
      <Case>
        <When>
          <True/>
        </When>
        <Then>
          <Dependency path="/vaAgeDeductionAllowed"/>
        </Then>
      </Case>
    </Switch>
  </Derived>
</Fact>

facts.name: City or county the filer lived in on January 1, 2025
facts.description: Form 760 header, "Locality Code"; 2024 instructions page 14: "the locality in which you lived on January 1, 2025 ... Local school funding is allocated based in part on this information." Asked and confirmed by the filer: the federal address gives a city name and a ZIP, but a ZIP can straddle localities and the date is the day after the tax year. When the ZIP lies in one locality, website-static/js/virginia-locality.js fills this in from it, and the filer confirms it.
facts.rawXml:
<Fact path="/vaLocality">
  <Name>City or county the filer lived in on January 1, 2025</Name>
  <Description>Form 760 header, "Locality Code"; 2024 instructions page 14: "the locality in which you
        lived on January 1, 2025 ... Local school funding is allocated based in part on this
        information." Asked and confirmed by the filer: the federal address gives a city name and a
        ZIP, but a ZIP can straddle localities and the date is the day after the tax year. When the
        ZIP lies in one locality, website-static/js/virginia-locality.js fills this in from it, and
        the filer confirms it.</Description>
  <Writable>
    <Enum optionsPath="/vaLocalityOptions"/>
  </Writable>
</Fact>

facts.description: 2024 Form 760 instructions, Line 33: the instructions offer a lookup table for totals under $1,000 and a worksheet above that; this prototype applies the rate directly.
facts.rawXml:
<Fact path="/vaUntaxedPurchases">
  <Name>Total of purchases on which no Virginia sales tax was paid</Name>
  <Description>2024 Form 760 instructions, Line 33: the instructions offer a lookup table for totals
        under $1,000 and a worksheet above that; this prototype applies the rate directly.</Description>
  <Writable>

facts.name: Form 760 Line 33, consumer's use tax
facts.description: The untaxed purchases times the rate for the filer's locality (/vaUseTaxRate in the virginiaLocalities module), rounded to the dollar; $0 when the filer had no untaxed purchases.
facts.rawXml:
<Fact path="/vaUseTax">
  <Name>Form 760 Line 33, consumer's use tax</Name>
  <Description>The untaxed purchases times the rate for the filer's locality
        (/vaUseTaxRate in the virginiaLocalities module), rounded to the dollar; $0 when the filer had
        no untaxed purchases.</Description>
  <Derived>
    <Switch>
      <Case>
        <When>
          <Dependency path="/vaHasUntaxedPurchases"/>
        </When>
        <Then>
          <Round>
            <Multiply>
              <Dependency module="virginiaLocalities" path="/vaUseTaxRate"/>
              <Dependency path="/vaUntaxedPurchases"/>
            </Multiply>
          </Round>
        </Then>
      </Case>
      <Case>
        <When>
          <True/>
        </When>
        <Then>
          <Dollar>0</Dollar>
        </Then>
      </Case>
    </Switch>
  </Derived>
</Fact>

<Fact path="/vaDeclaration">

  <Description>A single USWDS checkbox (a multi-enum with one option, the only checkbox the
        runtime renders) carrying the Form 760 declaration as its label. Required: the sign screen
        cannot be left until it is checked, and js/virginia-sign.js refuses to send without it.</Description>
  <Writable>

facts.name: Form 760 Line 16, Virginia income tax
facts.description: The tax on whichever way of filing the return claims. Line 17 (the spouse tax adjustment) is out of scope, so Line 18 equals Line 16.
facts.rawXml:
<Fact path="/vaTax">
  <Name>Form 760 Line 16, Virginia income tax</Name>
  <Description>The tax on whichever way of filing the return claims. Line 17 (the spouse tax
        adjustment) is out of scope, so Line 18 equals Line 16.</Description>
  <Derived>
    <Switch>
      <Case>
        <When>
          <Dependency module="virginiaCredits" path="/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit"/>
        </When>
        <Then>
          <Dependency path="/vaWithCreditTax"/>
        </Then>
      </Case>
      <Case>
        <When>
          <True/>
        </When>
        <Then>
          <Dependency path="/vaWithoutCreditTax"/>
        </Then>
      </Case>
    </Switch>
  </Derived>
</Fact>
